message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge a security deposit, but it cannot exceed **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit or **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a separate account and returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Get a written receipt and keep copies of all receipts for repairs or cleaning.
• Ask for a written itemized list of deductions if the landlord keeps part of the deposit. | | **Habitability / Repairs** | • Texas law requires landlords to maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition and to repair major defects (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical).
• If the landlord fails to make necessary repairs, you may withhold rent, pay for repairs yourself and deduct the cost, or terminate the lease. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or letter) and give a reasonable time to fix the issue.
• Keep records of all communications and any repair invoices. | | **Rent Payment & Late Fees** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Landlords may charge a late fee, but it must be reasonable and stated in the lease. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Eviction Process** | • A landlord must give you a written notice before filing an eviction:
 • **3‑Day Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (if rent is overdue).
 • **30‑Day Notice to Vacate** (for month‑to‑month leases).
 • **60‑Day Notice to Vacate** (for longer leases or if the landlord wants to end the tenancy).
• After the notice period, the landlord can file a lawsuit in court. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• If you receive a notice, you can contest it in court by showing that the landlord violated the lease or the law. | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries and check that the notice was given. | | **Discrimination** | • Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas statutes, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | • Report any discriminatory practices to the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Termination** | • You can terminate a lease early by giving proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month).
• Some leases allow “early termination” clauses that require a fee. | • Review your lease for any early‑termination fees or conditions. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Many leases prohibit subletting without landlord approval.
• If you want to sublet, get written permission. | • Keep a copy of the approval and any related agreements. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If a landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Commission on Human Rights, or HUD.
• You may also sue for damages or seek a court order to compel repairs. | • Document everything (photos, receipts, emails). | ### Quick Resources | Resource | What it offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | File complaints against landlords, find consumer guides. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | File discrimination complaints. | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | Fair Housing complaints, guidance. | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Free legal clinics, workshops. | | **Texas Property Code** | The statutory text governing landlord‑tenant relations. | --- #### Bottom line - **Know your lease**: read it carefully and keep a copy. - **Document everything**: receipts, notices, communication. - **Act promptly**: respond to notices, report problems early. - **Seek help when needed**: use the resources above or consult an attorney. If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a notice you received, or a repair issue), let me know and I can give more tailored guidance.
